The most likely corrupted element is **Mst2**. Its sensitivity is the largest of the startup-branch devices for line regulation (-2.42% for +20%), and its operating point is abnormal: it sinks 1.597 µA, about 16x the core current, with Vgs (0.647 V) barely above Vth (0.633 V). That is consistent with a short, wide device (W=2, L=0.5) where a longer, weaker device was intended. Mst1 is second because it has the matching positive sensitivity (+2.52%) and sources the same 1.6 µA. Mst3 is third because it is the startup kick device whose turn-on governs whether the core escapes the zero state.

```json
{"ranking": ["Mst2", "Mst1", "Mst3"], "fault": "Mst2 (startup-branch NMOS, gate=vref) is sized too strong/short: W=2 um, L=0.5 um instead of a longer, weaker device. It sinks about 1.6 uA from node st, which loads the startup branch, degrades line regulation, and prevents reliable start-up. Restore a longer-channel, weaker size so it conducts only when vref is near its nominal value."}
```
